content.user_title: Evaluate LLM Agents with Reliable Tests
content.value_statement: LLM agents can pass simple checks while failing real workflows. This skill helps build behavioral tests, benchmarks, and monitoring for stronger production evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Design statistical evaluation runs for nondeterministic agent outputs.
Define behavioral contract tests for agent invariants.
Create capability assessments and benchmark plans for LLM agents.
Identify anti-patterns such as single-run testing and string-only matching.
Plan reliability metrics and regression testing for production agents.
limitations: Does not provide an executable benchmark harness.
Does not include ready-made datasets or scoring tools.
Requires domain-specific success criteria from the user.
Cannot guarantee production performance from benchmark results alone.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Gates
use_cases.description: Create repeatable checks before shipping a new agent version.

use_cases.title: Measure Capability Coverage
use_cases.description: Map agent tasks to benchmarks, contracts, and reliability metrics.

use_cases.title: Monitor Production Behavior
use_cases.description: Track regressions, flaky outcomes, and metric gaming after deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner plan for a new agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evaluation plan for an LLM agent that performs [task]. Include core behaviors, sample test cases, success criteria, and common failure modes.

prompt_templates.title: Define Behavioral Contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Define behavioral contract tests for an agent used in [workflow]. Focus on invariants, unacceptable actions, input boundaries, and review criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Design Statistical Benchmarks
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a statistical benchmark for an agent that can produce varied outputs. Include run counts, scoring dimensions, confidence thresholds, and handling for flaky results.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Production Regression Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production regression strategy for an LLM agent. Include pre-release gates, monitoring metrics, drift signals, incident review, and retraining data safeguards.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a customer support agent before release.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose behavioral contracts for escalation, refusal handling, tone, tool use, and answer accuracy. It would also recommend repeated runs to measure flaky outcomes.

output_examples.input: Check whether a coding agent regressed after a model update.
output_examples.output: The skill would define task suites, compare pass distributions, review failure categories, and separate model behavior changes from environment issues.

output_examples.input: Reduce benchmark gaming in an internal agent scorecard.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend multiple scoring dimensions, hidden evaluation sets, production-aligned tasks, and checks for leakage from prompts or training data.

best_practices: Run each evaluation multiple times and compare outcome distributions.
Test behavioral invariants instead of exact output strings.
Separate benchmark scores from production readiness decisions.
anti_patterns: Relying on a single successful run as evidence of reliability.
Testing only happy paths while ignoring adversarial inputs.
Optimizing one metric until it no longer reflects user value.

faq.question: What does this skill help evaluate?
faq.answer: It helps evaluate LLM agents through behavioral tests, benchmarks, capability checks, and reliability metrics.

faq.question: Can it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides evaluation guidance and test design, but it does not include an executable test runner.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How does it handle nondeterministic agent outputs?
faq.answer: It recommends repeated runs, distribution analysis, and success criteria that allow valid output variation.

faq.question: Is it only for benchmark design?
faq.answer: No. It also covers behavioral contracts, regression checks, reliability metrics, and production monitoring.

faq.question: What input should users provide?
faq.answer: Users should provide the agent task, target workflow, known risks, success criteria, and production constraints.
